raw_response:
I've been farming these 9 mu for 30 years. Never went to school, but I know my land. My son and daughter-in-law work at the garment factory in town, so it's mostly me and my old man handling the fields, though they come back to help at harvest if the boss gives them leave. Money is always tight — we need cash for my grandson's school fees, so I can't go buying the fanciest inputs. But I also can't afford a bad harvest, so I stick with what works.

**Wheat** — I plant the whole 9 mu in winter wheat, same as always, around October 8th to 10th, right after National Day when the weather cools down. I save my own seed from last year — good plump kernels, why pay the seed shop? I plow the field first, then broadcast about 50 jin of compound fertilizer per mu before planting. At Qingming, when the wheat is jointing and if it looks a bit yellow, I spread another 30 to 35 jin of urea per mu. My neighbor Lao Wang uses a bit more, but his son sends him more money from Beijing. I water three times if the well doesn't run dry — once before winter if it's too dry, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. For spraying, I put down herbicide in early spring when the weeds first show, and if aphids come like they did two years ago, I'll spray insecticide too. Last year I got about 800 jin per mu; this year I'm hoping for the same, maybe 850 jin if the spring rain is good.

**Maize** — The wheat comes off in early June, and we have no time to waste. I buy hybrid seed from the shop in town — yellow dent, the kind everyone plants, about 4 jin per mu. Costs more than wheat seed, but you can't save hybrid seed, it doesn't grow right the second year. We usually hire the tractor-plower for a quick pass, then plant right away, sometimes the same day. I put 40 to 50 jin of compound fertilizer per mu in the planting holes. At big trumpet stage, if the leaves look pale, I might spread a little urea, but I don't always — maize doesn't need as much fussing as wheat. I irrigate twice: once right after planting if the soil is dry, and once when the tassels come out. One round of herbicide after planting, that's usually enough. Harvest is in late September, and I hope for 900 jin per mu, though last year it was closer to 850 because of the dry August.

Labor is mostly us two old folks. At wheat harvest and maize harvest, we might hire 2-3 days of casual labor from the village — young men charge 150 yuan a day now, so I avoid it when I can. My daughter-in-law helped plant the maize last year, but I don't know if she can get off work this June.
